dedupe_keys.name: internet atlas geographic database of internet physical infrastructure pops and links

description: Internet Atlas is a geographic database of the physical internet, built by Ramakrishnan Durairajan, Subhankar Ghosh, Xin Tang and Paul Barford at the University of Wisconsin-Madison with Brian Eriksson of Technicolor, and described in the paper 'Internet Atlas: A Geographic Database of the Internet' at the ACM HotPlanet workshop in 2013. The team compiled it by searching network operators' published maps, websites and filings for points of presence (PoPs), data centres, exchange points and the conduits linking them, then geocoding and digitising them. At the time of the paper it held over 9,500 PoPs and about 13,500 links for more than 270 networks, and was served through an ArcGIS-based web portal that overlaid the infrastructure on other layers such as hazards and transport routes. The data underpinned later studies of US long-haul fibre ('InterTubes') and of sea-level-rise risk to internet infrastructure. Coverage: mainly the United States, with global networks included. Format and access: GIS layers through a web portal, with licence and cost not stated in the paper; the portal (internetatlas.org) could not be reached from this session, so current availability is unknown. Caveats: compiled from public maps of varying accuracy; the snapshot ages as networks change. Simulation uses: exposure of PoPs and long-haul links to floods, sea-level rise and other hazards, and network models of the physical internet for failure studies. Related records: the Lights Out sea-level-rise case study used these data, and the Internet Topology Zoo and CAIDA datasets cover network topology.
